The defense offer has strong structural terms: automatic payments, no clear sailing, and any unawarded fee going to the class. A $28 million fund is meaningful against the class’s litigation risk, but the case has substantial potential value and direct distribution makes the fund especially effective. Counter at $38 million plus $9 million in fees, preserving the favorable structural terms, while leaving room to negotiate. Do not accept yet.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The parties negotiated directly. In Round 1, class counsel proposed a $40 million class fund and $10 million in attorneys’ fees, with automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and any unawarded fees going to the class. Defense counsel then proposed a $27 million class fund and $5.5 million in fees, retaining those distribution and fee protections. In Round 2, class counsel accepted that proposal, subject to court approval. The resulting settlement provides a $27 million class fund, $5.5 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses subject to court approval, automatic payments to identified class members, no clear-sailing provision, and no reversion to Brightline of fees the court declines to award.
